ESA WorldCover land cover

geo_landcover.Rd

geo_landcover() reads the ESA WorldCover 10 m global land-cover map (Zanaga et al. 2022) for an area, straight from its public cloud-optimised GeoTIFFs (3 x 3 degree tiles on AWS; also served as the "esa-worldcover" collection of the Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC API, see geo_stac_search()). Only the window over the area is read.

Classes: 10 tree cover, 20 shrubland, 30 grassland, 40 cropland, 50 built-up, 60 bare or sparse vegetation, 70 snow and ice, 80 permanent water, 90 herbaceous wetland, 95 mangroves, 100 moss and lichen.

Usage

geo_landcover(area, classes = NULL, template = NULL, year = 2021)

geo_worldcover_tiles(bbox)

Arguments

area

Area: sf, sfc, SpatVector, SpatRaster, SpatExtent or c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) in degrees.

classes

Optional class codes to keep, for example c(10, 95) for forest (tree cover and mangroves). The result is then TRUE for those classes and FALSE elsewhere.

template

Optional SpatRaster (for example a DEM) whose grid the result should share. Land cover is resampled to it with the modal class ("mode"), reading coarser overviews when the template is coarser than 10 m.

year

2021 (version 200, default) or 2020 (version 100).

bbox

c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) in degrees.

Value

A SpatRaster of class codes, or a logical layer with classes.

geo_worldcover_tiles(): tile names such as "S09E144" (the south-west corner of each 3 x 3 degree tile).

References

Zanaga, D. et al. (2022). ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200. doi:10.5281/zenodo.7254221

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive() && rlang::is_installed("terra")
forest <- geo_landcover(c(146.5, -6.6, 146.7, -6.4), classes = c(10, 95))
}
